SI needs a competitor. Because it's clear at this point they have no desire to advance the game.

OK, So it's FM, you will get your money's worth. But FM23 is not a good vintage. I have given it a thumbs up - because of the value it offers, but it is a very reluctant thumbs up.

I got over 1000 hours out of FM 22, and felt that was a poor year. Initial reaction (30 hours of beta) is this year is worse still (by worse i mean fewer changes and less improvements on the previous years).

Some of the new features are nice , i like the fan info/expectations, i quite like the end of season manager timeline (which i wasn't expecting to), but neither of these are game changing. However, that's about where the good ends for the new features.

The scouting changes are clunky, and make it feel more awkward to set up (and also don't work some of the time, but i will put this down to actual bugs in the beta, rather than design, and hope i am right). Also the old system still is there for some competitions for some reason, just to add to the confusion.

The squad planner is a good idea, but poorly implemented (and the layout for it is god awful - hopefully skins will help here). I keep just going back to the squad depth view as used in previous version, only it now takes me 3 more clicks to get there from my squad page.

Player traits are nearly impossible to see anymore, because SI choose to put them in the world's smallest box on the player screen for some reason - again skins may come to the rescue here.

In game changes/ match engine, improvements are noticeable, but small (you will loose the ball in midfield more often, and the AI won't wait until the 72nd minute to change their tactic against you any more), but overall feels very similar to FM22. I heard a lot about the game being harder - its not. As always with FM (and i don't say this as a bad thing) difficulty is down to the team you choose/ restrictions you give yourself.

For a game i know i will still play ~1000 hours of, i am disappointed. I knew the changes were small from the feature videos/release notes etc, however even those "new" features they have introduced in FM 23 are either poorly done and/or not very impactful on the game itself.
I understand why FM 21/22 were weak years, but i had hoped they would get their act together for FM23. However i was wrong,

As always, FM is fantastic value - it offers hundred of hours of replayability and is one of my favourite games, but this year really is just a glorified database update.

I've bought every FM since 2015 and this is my last. It makes me laugh when I hear the backlash EA and other developers get regarding adding little changes to their game franchises as Sports Interactive have been robbing their fan base for the last 5 or so years. They pump out an exact copy and paste each year for a whopping AUD $80 price tag and add a new feature here and there but NEVER address the bugs and issues that fans having been begging to be fixed for years. Admittedly there's little they could add to the game, the features are there but some are just laughably bad, bugged out, or completely broken.

The first issue is the [b] dialogue options and player interaction [/b] during individual and team meeting conversations. The choices you have when trying to have a simple conversation with one of your players is laughable. You have about four options to choose from but they always end in two outcomes. One you either bend over backwards and promise a mediocre/crap player more playing time or a new contract even though they probably don't deserve it. The second direction you can go is say no to the player in which they will have a tantrum and start yelling to the media and their teammates about how much you suck as a manager, even though that player has an average rating of 6.4.

Team meetings are even worse! The dialogue options are not only poor when it comes to choice, they're completely broken. My team was 10 games unbeaten, top of the table and had a 10-point gap between us and second place. I decided to have a team meeting as to avoid potential complacency, I chose the option "We've been in great form, lets keep it going and ensure we can win the title". My players responded with "That's being too ambitious" and then their morale plummeted in which I lost the gap and inevitably missed out on promotion. We were strong favorites in the win the title and you expect me to believe they didn't have the confidence in themselves to win the league? To say it in one sentence, dialogue and player interaction sucks in this game!

Also a side note, why are my three dialogue options at the end of the season team meeting only covering when I want my players back in pre-season? I couldn't care less about pre-season, I want to rip my players a new hole for dropping the ball right at the end of the current season, not next season. IMPROVE YOUR DIALOGUE OPTIONS.

The second issue is the [b] media [/b]. I've seen some repetitive features in games but my god this takes the throne. Yet again it seems Sports Interactive struggle to make a decent feature that involves interaction between the player and an NPC. Every signing, every match, every injury, you will deal with the exact same copy and paste meaningless questions from the media that rarely impact the game. I attend the main press conferences in pre-season but then usually skip the rest, I don't want to repeat myself constantly.

The third and main issue with this game is the [b] injury system [/b]. Horrific. The most unrealistic and garbage portion of this game is the never-ending constant bombardment of injuries that you will face. No matter what I have changed or tweaked I never seem to go a season without 30+ injuries. 5-10 would be acceptable but in this game it's just ridiculous. Hire the best physios the world has to offer? Nope. Reduce the intensity of training to lower injury risk? Nope. It is not realistic that players are snapping ankles, breaking legs, and breaking ribs week-in week-out.

Until Sports Interactive address issues that have been present in their game since around FM 2018, they're going to continue to bleed fans. START ADDRESSING YOUR ISSUES!

Football Manager, the game that makes you question your life choices and wonder if you should've pursued a career in sports management instead of whatever it is you're currently doing. It's like having a part-time job, but instead of a paycheck, you get the satisfaction of guiding your virtual team to glory. And by glory, I mean avoiding relegation.

The game starts innocently enough, with you choosing your favorite team, or perhaps a struggling lower league side that you hope to take to the Premier League. You'll find yourself drawn into the world of tactics, transfers, and temperamental players faster than you can say "sacked in the morning."

Your first task is to figure out the tactics, and this is where you realize that the beautiful game is also the most complicated. It's like trying to solve a Rubik's Cube while blindfolded and wearing oven mitts. You'll mess around with formations, roles, and instructions, hoping to stumble upon that magical combination that turns your bunch of misfits into a winning machine.

And then there are the transfers. You'll spend more time negotiating contracts and scouting potential players than you'll care to admit. You'll have a notebook filled with wonderkids from obscure countries and a growing disdain for agents who think they can demand a private jet for their client.

The match days are where the real stress sets in. You'll watch the games unfold with bated breath, hoping that your tactical genius pays off. When things go well, you'll feel like a footballing genius. But when your star striker misses an open goal for the tenth time, you'll question why you ever decided to manage a football club in the first place.

The press conferences and player interactions are where you'll hone your skills in diplomacy. One wrong word, and you could have a mutiny on your hands. Praise your players too much, and their heads will swell faster than a hot air balloon. Criticize them, and you'll have a full-blown crisis on your hands. It's like juggling fragile egos while walking on a tightrope.

But despite all the stress and frustration, there's something undeniably addictive about Football Manager. The thrill of finding that hidden gem of a player, the satisfaction of getting a lower league team promoted, and the heartache of a last-minute defeat in the cup final – it's all part of the rollercoaster that is football management.

In conclusion, Football Manager is not just a game; it's a way of life. It's a test of your tactical prowess, your negotiating skills, and your ability to handle pressure. It's the only game where you can be simultaneously adored and vilified by virtual fans, where you can achieve greatness or experience heartbreak, all from the comfort of your computer. So, if you've ever dreamed of being the next Sir Alex Ferguson or Arsène Wenger, here's your chance. Just don't forget to save before that crucial Champions League final.

This should not be called Football Manager 2023. This is Football Manager 2021.8. That is it. I usually place around 1000 to 3000 hours per FM game.

Last years version saw very very few changes from FM21 so I recorded barely 400 hours on it. This years game? I mean...its more polished? Whoope!

So lets start with the good. 


GOOD : 

Supporters vision : Fantastic addition I actually really like it worthy of being called "a new Feature"
Smooth gameplay : Looks and plays smoother then last year
Manager face graphics : Looks way better and it was actually improved
New Animations : They look great! Players can dance now!

BAD : 

Set Pieces : Not been touched in close to 10 years. No additions same crap, and they are so often exploited in tactics because of how ancient they are.

International Management : You are releasing a game in the same month as there is a World Cup...how can you not use this opportunity to make something great...unreal!

Tactics : You changed the names of few things so it looks news. BRAVO! Same thing as it has been for years.

Graphics: LMA Manager 2007 looks better than this game. I understand you don't want to make the game too graphically taxing but you have low, medium, high, and ultra settings. Use it properly!!

Sound : Sound has not been updated in 20 years. It's awful, generic, and boring. Not to mention the sound slider does not work properly at best of times.

Draw changes : I am sorry...WHO ASKED FOR THIS ?!?! It just looks sorry but stupid! You changed the wrong things! Draws were fine. You did not need to make them extra special...even then now it's just clunky and confusing at best.

Manager Pathway: Again. WHO ASKED FOR THIS?! HOW CAN THIS BE LAUDED AS A HEADLINE FEATURE? You should have added a feature where you can mold your character's history like what clubs did he play for? Why he retired and became a manager? We are not asking you to go the FIFA Manager route and give your entire life and stuff. We want new stuff that can be as simple as your manager's history.

Whoever greenlit releasing the game like this. With barely any changes. Knowing people will buy it in drowes should be SACKED. This is unacceptable. I have given you a pass for the last two years due to COVID.

As someone who owns 2015, 16, 19, 20, 21, 22 and now 23. I am part of the problem.

TLDR: For someone new to the series, you will get just as much enjoyment out of 2021 or 2022 and miss out on very little in terms of features. 

In general, I love the series, but each year I feel the "buyer's remorse" more and more. I'm sure it has been a tough time for development of the last couple of years, but the features / updates to the game, compared with the previous year, are hard to justify the purchase, particularly at launch.

One thing I feel SI should be utilizing more is optional, free DLC. For example, a DLC pack of (say) 60,000 photo realistic / generated faces, which would take the place of any missing faces and be used in place of the very dated-looking Newgen / Regen faces? As OPTIONAL DLC, this would in no way impact the people who have been playing since 2005 and are somehow still using the same laptop to this day?

Similarly, there could be a DLC pack for custom / create a team options (badges, kits, kit sponsors etc), there are many more areas where optional DLC would improve the feel and look of the game also, and have no impact to the people running the game on an Atari 'woody'.

I would like to take this time to thank the community who tirelessly put in hours and hours, working on mods and graphical improvements, to give us a better game. We should not have to rely on these people as much as we do!
